guidelines.title: named button type map
guidelines.rule: Named type map — Default = non-primary, safe if unsure. Primary = complete/recommend. Text = low emphasis (e.g. table actions). Icon-only must have a Tooltip. Text+icon = supplementary meaning. Dashed = add content in an area. Link = external links. Ghost = dark or colored background. (Primary ≤1 per button group is named here, not a second row — dual-cite Actions/Atlassian/Carbon by scope.)

citation.source: Ant Design — Button spec ; Ant Design — Button

pass_when: Button type matches that map; icon-only has a tooltip; at most one primary in a button group.
fail_when: Type used off-map (e.g. link for an in-app action, dashed for a primary complete); icon-only with no tooltip; two primaries in one group.
guidelines.do_not_claim: One global primary cap for page/section (`actions.buttons.one_primary`); that a tooltip replaces always-visible text (`actions.icons.always_visible_text_label`). Overlap with Actions 40: `actions.buttons.one_primary` (page/view). Dual-cite by cited scope; do not invent one global cap.

guidelines.title: never two icons in one button
guidelines.rule: Never two icons in one button.
pass_when: A button has zero or one icon.
fail_when: Two icons in one button.
guidelines.do_not_claim: Icon+text supplementary meaning as this row.

guidelines.title: danger cancel primary when not recommended
guidelines.rule: If the user's intention is delete, use danger to warn. If the system does not recommend the deletion, set Cancel as the primary action. Compatible with "primary not destructive"; dual-cite, don't collapse.
pass_when: Delete uses danger warning. When the system does not recommend deletion, Cancel is the primary; destructive is not the recommended/primary.
fail_when: Delete is primary when the system does not recommend it; or danger/primary collapsed so destructive is the recommended path.
guidelines.do_not_claim: A second invented rule beyond this cite + `actions.buttons.default_not_destructive`. Overlap with Actions 40: `actions.buttons.default_not_destructive`.

guidelines.title: one cta per screen
guidelines.rule: One Call to Action per screen — CTA usually appears alone, command-like (landing/welcome); may be as wide as its parent. Distinct from one-primary-in-a-group.
pass_when: Landing/welcome (command-like) screen has one CTA, usually alone; may span its parent.
fail_when: Multiple CTAs on that landing/welcome screen.
guidelines.do_not_claim: One invented global cap vs group / page / section; `actions.buttons.one_primary` as a delete of this named CTA-per-screen row.

guidelines.title: footer buttons when body cannot carry
guidelines.rule: Footer buttons when the body can't carry them — collapsed/hidden content (not one screen), or complex body with subgroup actions so Complete is not confused with local actions. Footer = separation from body.
pass_when: Complete/footer actions sit in the footer when content is collapsed/not one screen, or when a complex body has subgroup actions.
fail_when: Complete sits among local subgroup actions so it is confused with them, on a body that cannot carry the page action.
guidelines.do_not_claim: Always-footer as a house default.

guidelines.title: conversation vs navigation order
guidelines.rule: Conversation: ask for the needed/desired action, then present risks. Navigation: Back on the left (previous step). Less important actions go right or bottom. Collapsed overflow content stays on the right.
pass_when: Conversation order is desired action then risks. Navigation has Back on the left. Less important / overflow sit right or bottom as cited.
fail_when: Risks before the needed action in a conversation pattern; Back not on the left in navigation; overflow collapsed to the left.
guidelines.do_not_claim: A global web OK/Cancel order (`actions.buttons.follow_platform_ok_cancel_order`).

guidelines.title: group spacing overflow dropdown
guidelines.rule: Flush groups look like a Toggle. Align in one line with spaces. Same group: no dividers. Different groups: space or a divider. If more than three operations: 1 primary + n secondary, extra into a Dropdown.
pass_when: Related actions are spaced (not flush-as-toggle); same group has no divider; different groups use space or a divider; more than three operations use 1 primary + secondaries, extras in a Dropdown.
fail_when: Flush non-toggle groups; dividers inside one group; more than three operations left in one undifferentiated strip.
guidelines.do_not_claim: A house cap other than Ant's "more than three" / Tidwell "three or four". Overlap with Actions 40: `actions.button_groups`.

guidelines.title: ok cancel default vs explicit verb
guidelines.rule: OK / Cancel as Ant default labels (CONFLICT). Spec still defaults to OK/Cancel but also: use a verb; describe the result (Publish, Login); if primary is negative, stress consequences (Delete / Cancel). Dual-cite vs NN/g `explicit_verb_not_ok`. Do not pick a winner. Prefer cited verb-names-the-outcome as pass when both apply; Ant default is a conflict flag, not a second invented rule.

citation.source: Ant Design — Button spec ; NN/g — UI Copy

pass_when: When both cites apply, the primary names the outcome (Publish, Login, Delete); if primary is negative, the pair stresses consequences (Delete / Cancel).
fail_when: Generic OK where a specific verb is available and treated as satisfying the verb-names cite; or a house "always OK/Cancel" / "never OK" that deletes the other cite.
guidelines.do_not_claim: Collapsing Ant's named default into a second invented rule, or deleting `actions.copy.explicit_verb_not_ok`. Overlap with Actions 40: `actions.copy.explicit_verb_not_ok`.

guidelines.title: label left default vs top
guidelines.rule: Ant: label left of input by default; top when the text is too long or in English context; consistent within the system. Dual-cite Fluent/Spectrum top-default. Do not pick a winner.
pass_when: Labels are consistently left or consistently top in-product (Ant left-default; Fluent/Spectrum top-default). Ant also allows top when label text is too long or in English context.
fail_when: Mixed left/top in one form with no reason; or a house default that bans the other cite.
guidelines.do_not_claim: A house left-or-top winner; GOV.UK sentence-case/no-colons as this placement row. Overlap with extra 73: `fluent.labels-top-aligned-by-default`. Overlap with Forms 54: beyond LIVE `visible_label` / `label_stays_visible`.

guidelines.title: radio count 2 to 5
guidelines.rule: Radio count — must be more than two, normally fewer than five (all options visible to compare). Dual-cite NN/g handful/dropdown cutoff; Ant names the 2–5 band.
pass_when: Radios are used for more than two and normally fewer than five visible options.
fail_when: Radios for two-or-fewer as this Ant band, or a long set as radios when Ant would use dropdown (>5).
guidelines.do_not_claim: One house cutoff vs NN/g handful / Polar <4 / USWDS <7 / M3 6 / Carbon 3. Overlap with extra 73: `nng.too-few-options-radios-not-dropdown` / `polar.select-4plus-choice-list-under-4`. Overlap with Forms 54: `forms.inputs.match_control_and_size`, `dropdown_chooser`, `combo_box`, `offer_choices_not_only_text`.

guidelines.title: checkbox vs switch
guidelines.rule: Checkbox often with a submit for state; a single checkbox can be two-state. Switch takes effect immediately and does not need a button. Dual-cite Lightning toggle-immediate; Ant names Switch vs checkbox pairing.
pass_when: Switch applies immediately with no submit. Checkbox state waits for submit when it is part of a submitted form; a single checkbox may be two-state.
fail_when: Switch that does nothing until a separate submit; or a form checkbox that applies immediately as if it were Switch.
guidelines.do_not_claim: A house "all toggles immediate" beyond the two cites.

guidelines.title: dropdown when over 5 no truncate
guidelines.rule: Dropdown when >5 — logical sort; option text fully displayed. Dual-cite NN/g dropdown band; this is Ant's cutoff + no-truncate.
pass_when: A >5 set uses a dropdown (on this Ant surface), options logically sorted, text fully displayed.
fail_when: >5 as a radio list on this Ant surface, truncated option text, or unsorted dump.
guidelines.do_not_claim: A house winner vs NN/g ~5–10 / combobox ~15+ / GOV.UK select-last-resort. Overlap with extra 73: `nng.dropdown-ok-narrow-middle` / `nng.too-many-combobox-not-long-dropdown` / `govuk.select-last-resort`.

guidelines.title: slider intensity grade
guidelines.rule: Slider = intensity/grade (volume, brightness, saturation) when a precise number is not required; pair NumberInput with Slider when precision is required.
pass_when: Slider is used for intensity/grade without a required precise number; precision uses Slider + NumberInput.
fail_when: Slider as the only control when a precise number is required; or slider for a non-intensity discrete choice.
guidelines.do_not_claim: GOV.UK "don't use range sliders" on question pages as a winner; MUI/Apple number-entry dual-cite as this slider row.

guidelines.title: settings mode and grouping thresholds
guidelines.rule: One mode per page: Instant Effect or Submission Effect (use submit when items interdepend). Item count: <7 no grouping; 7–15 group; >15 tab grouping.
pass_when: A settings page is one mode (instant or submission). Counts follow <7 / 7–15 / >15 tab grouping. Interdependent items use submission.
fail_when: Instant and submission mixed on one page; or counts grouped against those bands.
guidelines.do_not_claim: A house number that replaces 7 / 15; Switch-immediate as this page-mode row.

guidelines.title: editable list pattern by field count
guidelines.rule: Editable-list pattern by field count — dynamic add/remove when items ≤3 and inputs need no separate titles; editable table 2–5; collapsible panel 6–8; drawer when >8.

citation.source: Ant Design — Data entry ; Ant Design — Form research

pass_when: Pattern matches the cited count band (≤3 add/remove; 2–5 table; 6–8 panel; >8 drawer).
fail_when: Drawer for ≤3, or add/remove-without-titles for >8, against those bands.
guidelines.do_not_claim: A house count that collapses the bands.

guidelines.title: no multi column form in one area
guidelines.rule: No multi-column form inside one area — vertical single column is the efficient default; weak grouping may put short related fields on one line, not a second reading column. Card grouping when content is usually more than two screens, each card with a large title.

citation.source: Ant Design — Data entry ; Ant Design — Form research

pass_when: One area is a single reading column (short related fields may share a line). Content usually more than two screens uses titled cards.
fail_when: Two reading columns of fields in one area; or >two-screens dump with no titled cards.
guidelines.do_not_claim: Forms keep-short / one-thing-per-page as a merge. Overlap with Forms 54: `forms.length.keep_short` / `forms.layout.single_column`.

guidelines.title: inline input feedback does not auto dismiss
guidelines.rule: Inline input feedback does not auto-dismiss — text follows the block; stays until the user performs the corresponding interaction.
pass_when: Inline input feedback stays until the corresponding interaction.
fail_when: Inline input feedback auto-dismisses.
guidelines.do_not_claim: Toast/Message auto-dismiss timings as this inline row.

guidelines.title: prefer undo or popconfirm over modal
guidelines.rule: Prefer undo (or Popconfirm) over Modal double-confirm — delete → success + Undo (message+undo gone after one minute or on Undo). If undo is invalid, use Popconfirm next to the control. Abusing Modal drops context and blocks undo. Dual-cite Primer "never warning when you mean undo" / NN/g undo; Ant names Popconfirm vs Modal.
pass_when: Delete uses success + Undo (gone after one minute or on Undo), or Popconfirm next to the control when undo is invalid — not a blocking Modal when undo would work.
fail_when: Modal double-confirm used where undo is valid; or no undo/Popconfirm on that delete.
guidelines.do_not_claim: Deleting `actions.confirm.serious_or_undo`; a house one-minute as law outside this cite. Overlap with Actions 40: `actions.confirm.serious_or_undo`. Overlap with extra 73: `nng.support-undo-discoverable`.

guidelines.title: message not for important failures
guidelines.rule: Message is not for important failures — Ant Message = top-centered, auto-dismiss (default 3s), non-blocking. Important failure → dialog with the reason. Do not use a lightweight prompt for important failure.
pass_when: Important failure uses a dialog with the reason. Lightweight Message is not used for that failure.
fail_when: Important failure only as a 3s top Message.
guidelines.do_not_claim: Spectrum toast ≥5s as a house winner over 3s; WCAG interruptions.

guidelines.title: dialog feedback only important actionable
guidelines.rule: Dialog feedback only for important, actionable information — centered, confirm/cancel to close, blocks other work. Avoid unnecessary reminders except failure. Dual-cite NN/g modal 7; Ant is the feedback-routing sentence.
pass_when: Blocking dialog is used for important actionable information / failure, not unnecessary reminders.
fail_when: Blocking dialog for a non-important reminder, or important actionable failure with no dialog when this routing applies.
guidelines.do_not_claim: Deleting `nng.modal-and-nonmodal-dialogs`; Spectrum toast-vs-dialog as a merge.

guidelines.title: hover detail overlay timing
guidelines.rule: Hover detail overlay timing — 0.5 s delay on mouseover; close immediately on mouse-out.

citation.source: Ant Design — Stay on the Page

pass_when: Detail overlay appears after 0.5 s hover; closes immediately on mouse-out.
fail_when: Instant open, delayed close, or no 0.5 s delay.
guidelines.do_not_claim: Click-outside input overlay (next row).

guidelines.title: input overlay click outside preserves
guidelines.rule: Input overlay: click outside preserves and closes.

citation.source: Ant Design — Stay on the Page

pass_when: Clicking outside an input overlay closes it and preserves the input.
fail_when: Click outside discards the input, or does not close.
guidelines.do_not_claim: Modal confirm Cancel-discards (MUI) as this overlay row.

guidelines.title: form in modal lifecycle
guidelines.rule: Form-in-Modal lifecycle — list-page "create" may popup a form in Modal. `destroyOnHidden` does not clear Form fields — call `resetFields`. `useForm` before open is disconnected unless `forceRender` (or equivalent). Prefer native submit; if the submit control is outside the Form (Modal footer), call `form.submit`.

citation.source: Ant Design — Form ; Ant Design — Modal

pass_when: Reopened create-modal form is reset (`resetFields`); form instance is connected when opened; footer submit still submits the Form (`form.submit` if outside).
fail_when: Stale fields after close (`destroyOnHidden` treated as reset); disconnected `useForm` without force-render; footer button that does not submit the Form.
guidelines.do_not_claim: API-table props beyond these named lifecycle facts; Polar "don't use modals for complex forms" as a winner.
